# RLT

[![CRAN
Version](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/RLT)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RLT)
[![CRAN
Downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/RLT?color=blue)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RLT)
[![GitHub
Version](https://img.shields.io/github/r-package/v/teazrq/RLT?label=GitHub&color=brightgreen)](https://github.com/teazrq/RLT)
[![R build
status](https://github.com/teazrq/RLT/actions/workflows/pkgdown.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/teazrq/RLT/actions)

**Reinforcement Learning Trees** is an R package for random forest
models with regression, classification, and survival analysis support.
The package uses a C++/Rcpp backend with OpenMP for parallel
computation.

[Website](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/) \|
[GitHub](https://github.com/teazrq/RLT) \|
[Issues](https://github.com/teazrq/RLT/issues)

## Highlights

- Regression, classification, and survival forests
- Reinforcement learning splits with embedded model guidance
- Linear combination splits for multivariate split directions
- Variable importance and random forest kernel utilities
- Survival prediction, confidence bands, and tree inspection tools
- Reproducible parallel fitting through recorded random seeds

The default fit uses ordinary single-variable splits. Set
`reinforcement = TRUE` to guide those splits with embedded models fitted
within nodes. Linear combination splits use a combined predictor
direction and are selected separately with `linear.comb > 1`; they do
not require reinforcement. The [Get Started
guide](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html) shows an
ordinary fit and a reinforced fit using the same data and settings.

## Installation

These guides describe **RLT source version 6.1.1**. The CRAN release is
a separate, older version whose interfaces and features may differ.
Source installation requires a C++ toolchain compatible with your R
installation. Set it up using the [platform
requirements](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html#platform-requirements),
then install the latest GitHub source into your normal shared R library:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("teazrq/RLT")
packageVersion("RLT")
```

GitHub installation uses the repository’s current default branch.
[`packageVersion()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/packageDescription.html)
checks the version number, which may be shared by different source
revisions. See [matching the documentation
revision](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html#match-the-documentation-revision)
when you need the exact source used by these guides.

The separate CRAN release can be installed with:

``` r

install.packages("RLT")
```

On Windows, use the matching
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/). For macOS and
Linux requirements, see the [installation
guide](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html). OpenMP
enables parallel computation; builds without it run serially. Windows
builds with and without OpenMP have been validated. macOS and Linux
source installation has not been verified for this documentation
revision.

## Quick Example

``` r

library(RLT)

set.seed(1)
n <- 200
p <- 6
x <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)
y <- x[, 1] - x[, 2] + rnorm(n)

fit <- RLT(
  x, y,
  model = "regression",
  ntrees = 100,
  importance = TRUE,
  seed = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

pred <- predict(fit, x[1:5, ])
pred$Prediction

importance(fit)
```

The five training rows illustrate the returned numeric predictions. To
evaluate prediction performance, use out-of-bag predictions or held-out
observations as in the [Get Started
analysis](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html#fit-and-evaluate-a-regression-forest).
`importance(fit)` reports how much the fitted forest relies on each
predictor.

## Documentation

Use the guides to install RLT, fit models, and interpret their
predictions:

- [Get Started](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/get-started.html):
  complete a first analysis
- [Regression
  Tutorial](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/regression-tutorial.html):
  predict a continuous response
- [Classification
  Tutorial](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/classification-tutorial.html):
  predict class labels and probabilities
- [Survival
  Tutorial](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/articles/survival-tutorial.html):
  analyze censored event times
- [Reference](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/index.html): look
  up arguments and returned values

## References

Cite the papers relevant to the methods used: Zhu et al. (2015) for
reinforcement learning trees, Xu et al. (2024) for matched-sample
variance estimation, and Formentini et al. (2022) for the CHF covariance
and Gaussian-simulation framework for survival bands.

- Zhu, R., Zeng, D., and Kosorok, M. R. (2015). Reinforcement Learning
  Trees. *Journal of the American Statistical Association*, 110(512),
  1770-1784. <https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2015.1036994>
- Xu, T., Zhu, R., and Shao, X. (2024). On variance estimation of random
  forests with Infinite-order U-statistics. *Electronic Journal of
  Statistics*, 18(1), 2135-2207. <https://doi.org/10.1214/24-EJS2247>
- Formentini, S. E., Liang, W., and Zhu, R. (2022). Confidence Band
  Estimation for Survival Random Forests. *arXiv preprint*,
  arXiv:2204.12038. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.12038>

# Package index

## Core Modeling Functions

Fit, predict, and print RLT models.

- [`RLT()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/RLT.md) :
  Reinforcement Learning Trees
- [`predict(`*`<RLT>`*`)`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/predict.RLT.md)
  : Predict with an RLT forest
- [`print(`*`<RLT>`*`)`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/print.RLT.md)
  : Print a RLT object

## Model Analysis and Utilities

Inspect fitted models, variable importance, kernels, and survival bands.

- [`importance()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/importance.md)
  : Variable Importance Summary
- [`print(`*`<importance.RLT>`*`)`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/print.importance.RLT.md)
  : Print Importance Summary
- [`forest.kernel()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/forest.kernel.md)
  : Compute a random forest kernel
- [`get.one.tree()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/get.one.tree.md)
  : Print a single tree
- [`get.surv.band()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/get.surv.band.md)
  : Construct survival confidence bands
- [`cindex()`](https://teazrq.github.io/RLT/reference/cindex.md) :
  C-index
